Tutorials

Learn TimeToAlign! step by step

These tutorials take you from zero to a working multimodal alignment, introducing one concept at a time. Each notebook uses real-world data from the project’s specimen collection and can be run locally after installing the library with pip install timetoalign[tutorial].

Prerequisites: Python 3.12+, basic familiarity with Jupyter notebooks.

Tutorial Notebooks

Title Description
Why TimeToAlign! Matters The problem of fragmented music data and how TimeToAlign! solves it
Core Concepts: Domains, Units, and Coordinates The three temporal domains and the six timeline types
Loading Data with TimeToAlign! Format-agnostic data ingestion with Loaders and EventStores
Loading Tabular Data CoordinateField, ComputedField, and custom loader configuration
Conversion Maps: Transforming Coordinates Unit transformations and coordinate conversion
Building Timelines: Events and Hierarchies Events, Segments, Children, and SegmentLines
Timestamps: Cross-Section Views Querying timeline hierarchies with TimeStamp and TimeIntervalStamp
Graphical Timelines TimeAxisPath, image-based timelines, and pixel-to-time conversion
Alignment Basics TimelineGroup, PerfectAlignment, and coordinate transfer
SUPRA Piano Roll: A Complete Alignment Workflow End-to-end alignment: IIIF images, ATON, MIDI, Audio, and Score
Beat Grids: Metrical Structure for Audio BeatGrid, FloorMap, RotationMap, and measure/beat queries
Multimodal Alignment: Beethoven Op. 18/4 IV AlignmentBundle, FlowMap, OMR, 16+ timelines across 3 domains
No matching items

Learning Path

The tutorials are designed to be followed in order:

  1. Foundations (00–03): What TimeToAlign! is, core concepts, loading data, and converting coordinates.
  2. Structure (04–05): Building timeline hierarchies and querying them with timestamps.
  3. Domains (06–07): Graphical timelines and alignment basics.
  4. Applications (08–10): Complete workflows on real datasets — a piano roll, beat grids, and a full multimodal Beethoven alignment.
